page.layout: One column of verse and headings, centred; running head and page number at the top; catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

p.i: Norica venturo Respublica Cæsare gaudens, Officium posuit testificata suum.
PARCERE subiectis, & debellare superbos, Convenit ingenio Cæsar inesse tuo, Sentiat optatam per te tua turba quietem, Subq; jugum per te barbarus hostis eat.
QVOD tibi tam cōstans faveat victoria Cæsar, Non modò Fortunæ muneris esse putà: Sacra sed augustum moderans Prudentia pectus, Hunc titulum laudis malunt esse suum.
SIC per te placidam capiat Germania pacem, Vt tibi nunc animis carminibusq; favet. Sic per te Geticus nostris à finibus hostis Pellatur, vires sensit ut ante tuas.
INTER opes tantas, inter tot regia sceptra, Quæ tu divino munere Cæsar habes; Temperat excelsam mitis moderatio mentem, Principe quid tanto dignius esse queat!

page.notes: Head "SVPRA IMAGINEM IV-STITIÆ." is set across two lines with a printed hyphen. The catchword in black letter is hard to read; reading "Andeut" is uncertain. The "q;" in "Subq;" and "carminibusq;" is a que-abbreviation with a mark that is hard to make out; copied as q;. Long s has been read as s throughout. The first stanza is the tail of a poem begun on the previous page. Small dots in the margins are not printed text and are left out.
